prompt.context: You are a consultant working for a bubble gum manufacturer. The CEO of the gum manufacturing company is concerned because his company is experiencing declining margin.
prompt.question: (1) What are the reasons behind the declining profitability? (2) What are your suggestions for improving profitability?

clarifying_info.q: Have sales been increasing or decreasing?
What are the main cost buckets?
clarifying_info.a: COGS (gum, sugar, flavor, smell, color), Labor, and SG&A.

clarifying_info.q: Have raw material unit costs changed?
clarifying_info.a: Raw material unit costs have not changed.

clarifying_info.q: What products does the company sell?
clarifying_info.a: Two types of gum: flavored and flavorless.

clarifying_info.q: Are the two products sold at the same price?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, both products are sold at the same price point.

clarifying_info.q: What raw materials go into each product?
clarifying_info.a: Flavored gum uses: gum, sugar, flavor, and color dye. Flavorless gum uses: gum, sugar, and color dye. The gum, sugar, and color dye components are the same size/quantity in both products.

framework: Diagnose revenue trend (sales volume, price, mix)
Diagnose cost trend (COGS components: raw materials by product, labor, SG&A)
Identify product mix shift between flavored and flavorless gum
Isolate the margin impact: same price, different cost structure per SKU
Generate profitability improvement options (short-term and long-term)

questions.prompt: Why is margin declining if sales are increasing and unit raw material costs are unchanged?
questions.guidance: The candidate should work through product mix. Sales are rising but both products are priced identically. Flavored gum requires an extra raw material (flavor) that flavorless gum does not. If the mix is shifting toward more flavored gum, total COGS per unit of revenue rises while revenue per unit stays flat, compressing margins. The root cause is a product-mix shift toward the higher-cost SKU at a price that does not reflect the cost difference.

questions.prompt: How would you improve the company's profitability?
questions.guidance: Strong answers present both short-term and long-term levers. Short-term (quick wins): (1) Raise the price of flavored gum to reflect its higher cost — acknowledge the risk that volume may fall and propose mitigants such as value-added variants (e.g., low-calorie flavored gum) or marketing to justify the premium. (2) Negotiate with existing flavor suppliers to reduce flavor input cost. (3) Source cheaper flavor raw materials from alternative suppliers. Long-term: (4) Vertically integrate by acquiring or partnering with a flavor manufacturing company to control flavor costs. When discussing price increases, interviewers may push on risk — candidate should address potential volume loss and propose promotional or product differentiation strategies.

brainstorming.prompt: What options exist for improving the profitability of the bubble gum manufacturer?

categories.name: Revenue / Pricing
ideas: Raise the price of flavored gum to reflect its higher raw material cost
Introduce a premium flavored gum line to justify higher price points
Bundle or upsell value-added variants (e.g., low-calorie, sugar-free flavored gum)
Invest in marketing and promotional efforts to support a price increase

categories.name: Cost Reduction — Short Term
ideas: Negotiate lower flavor input costs with existing suppliers
Dual-source or competitively bid the flavor ingredient across multiple suppliers
Reduce flavor intensity per unit if product specs allow
Improve manufacturing efficiency to lower labor cost per unit

categories.name: Cost Reduction — Long Term
ideas: Vertically integrate by acquiring a flavor manufacturing company
Form a joint venture with a flavor supplier to reduce cost and share risk
Invest in R&D to develop a proprietary low-cost flavor substitute

categories.name: Product Mix Management
ideas: Re-evaluate the product portfolio and rationalize SKUs
Promote flavorless gum more heavily to shift mix back toward the lower-cost product
Introduce tiered pricing across product lines to match price to cost structure

recommendation: The primary driver of declining margin is a product-mix shift toward flavored gum, which carries a higher raw material cost (the flavor ingredient) but is sold at the same price as flavorless gum — causing costs to rise while revenue per unit stays flat.

To restore profitability, the company should in the short term raise the price of flavored gum (with supporting marketing/value-added positioning) and negotiate or re-source the flavor input; in the long term, evaluate vertical integration of flavor manufacturing to structurally reduce cost.
risks: A flavored-gum price increase may cause volume loss if consumers trade down to flavorless or competitor products.
Vertical integration requires significant capital and execution capability outside the company's core competency.
Over-reliance on a single new flavor supplier could introduce supply-chain risk.
next_steps: Conduct price elasticity analysis on flavored gum to size the volume risk of a price increase.
Benchmark flavor input costs against industry peers and solicit competitive bids from alternative suppliers.
Assess financial and strategic feasibility of acquiring or partnering with a flavor manufacturer.
